- TCP is connection-oriented, requiring a handshake before data transfer, while UDP is connectionless and sends data without establishing a connection.
- TCP guarantees reliable delivery through acknowledgments, retransmissions, and sequencing, whereas UDP provides no guarantee that packets will arrive.
- TCP ensures packets arrive in order, while UDP packets may arrive out of order, duplicated, or not at all.
- TCP has higher overhead due to its larger header (20 bytes minimum) and connection management, while UDP has a smaller fixed header (8 bytes) and lower latency.
- TCP supports flow control and congestion control mechanisms, while UDP has neither, making it faster but potentially prone to network congestion.
